title: Continuous vantages: every training framing is shifted by a fresh random offset of up to ±12 px, so over an epoch the training views cover the ground continuously instead of standing on the fixed 24 m lattice
hypothesis: Champion exp 20 (0.0777): on held-out truedop_2024, usable 93.0%, false fix 0.75%, abstain 6.25%. The same eval viewpoints on the three training photographs score 100% usable / 0% false. Every position-sampling choice in this era has been the same: train.py shows each place only at the 72,712 exact lattice centres, 24 px apart, with heading as the only geometric variation. So each lattice framing appears three times per epoch (once per survey) at the same pixel-exact framing, over 8 epochs. A network with ~31 MB of weights can fit that discrete set of framings as framing-plus-survey fingerprints. That fit costs nothing on the training photographs (100%) but gives no structural invariance on a new photograph. Every eval view stands 11-17 m off-lattice, so on 2024 the model faces a new photograph AND an unseen framing at once. Its remaining abstentions are where the two members' beliefs stop agreeing. CLAUDE.md's Prignitz-detour record names this exact mechanism, continuous-vantage training with ±12 px jitter, as 'designed and implemented; never trained' and as the natural next move. That detour also showed that whatever fixes look-alike confusions has to act during training, not at decode time. This era has never touched how training positions are sampled; arch_json shows every change in exps 12-21 went to the trunk, head, augmentation pixels or weight schedule. Hypothesis: re-drawing each framing at a continuous random offset every time it is used makes any two uses of a place differ in framing. That removes the pixel-exact framing fingerprint as a solution and pushes both members toward the layout that survives a shift, which is also what survives a change of survey. The result should be more members agreeing on 2024, and so fewer abstentions. Note, stated plainly: with ±12 px jitter some training framings on the TRAINING photographs fall close to eval vantages. That is legitimate (deployment views are arbitrary vantages over mapped ground, and §4 says the model is shown all of its box), but it makes the logged train_capture_diagnostics less informative as a viewpoint test. The scored question, a never-seen photograph, is untouched: truedop_2024 is never loaded. Experiment 21 (LP-FT) is not re-run here. It died on a laptop DNS failure during its final epoch, so its verdict is void, but its training curves through epoch 7 matched exp 20's to the third decimal (top1 0.9062 vs 0.9056, xs_cos_same 0.783 vs 0.787), so a re-run is expected to land within noise.
method: model/train.py only. chunk_views() gains a per-position random offset (dx, dy), each drawn uniformly from the integers in [-12, +12] px (half the lattice stride). The offset is drawn once per position per use and SHARED across the three captures, the same way the heading is already shared, so the paired-survey design is kept. It is applied to the crop centre before cutting, and the targets (pos, cell_idx) are computed from the shifted centre. Shifted centres are clamped so the crop window stays inside the raster. Positions whose ±12 px jitter box could reach the region-holdout buffer get zero jitter (precomputed once), so the holdout diagnostic stays clean. Used in run_epoch and recalibrate_bn. survey_diag stays on the exact lattice. Nothing else changes: model.py, the losses, augmentation, MixStyle, committee, weight averaging, EPOCHS, and the export are all as in exp 20.
expected_outcome: mission_score 0.078 -> ~0.055-0.065: usable 93.0% -> ~94.5-95.5%, mostly from abstentions turning into usable fixes (abstain 6.25% -> ~4.5%), with false fix flat at ≤1.0%. Training-photograph diagnostics stay ~100% usable. Final training top1 (augmented, vs containing cell) may read 1-2 points lower than exp 20's 0.910, because shifted views sit nearer cell borders more often; that is expected and is not a regression. Refutation: if 2024 usable does not rise above 93.0%, then framing fingerprints were not what limited the new-photograph fixes. In that case the residual is purely photographic (survey content: season, construction, shadows), and the next lever is what the model sees, not where it stands. Wall time is unchanged (no extra compute per crop).
eli5: Until now the model studied Berlin from a fixed grid of spots 24 metres apart, the same spots every time, so it could partly memorise 'how this exact framing of this exact photo looks'. Now every time it studies a place, the camera is nudged a random few metres sideways first, so it never sees exactly the same picture twice. It has to learn what the place looks like, not what one framing looks like, and that should carry better to a photograph it has never seen.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: the 128 px frame is enlarged to 224 px and read by two independent copies of EfficientNet-B0 (pre-trained on ImageNet, Apache-2.0), fine-tuned on Berlin; each reads a 112-channel 14×14 map and a 320-channel 7×7 map, each lifted to 56 numbers and averaged over the frame into a 112-number place description; the weights carried are the average of the many versions visited over the second half of training

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: each extractor's description is centred, scaled to unit length and compared by angle against one unit-length reference direction per map tile (~3,000 tiles, 128 m each); the angle match times a fixed sharpness (30) is the tile score. The two members' tile-belief maps are averaged to pick the tile

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the averaged belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head per member that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot; the two nudges are averaged

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the SMALLER of the two members' belief on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — both navigators must independently back the same place; if either one spreads its belief elsewhere the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: NEW: continuous vantages. Every time a training spot is used, the camera is first shifted by a fresh random offset of up to ±12 m in each direction (the same shift in all three survey photographs, like the shared heading), so over an epoch the training views tile the ground continuously instead of standing on the fixed 24 m grid; the tile and offset targets follow the shifted position. Everything else as before: cross-survey style mixing, angular-margin tile loss, offset loss, paired three-survey batches, re-photographing augmentation, pre-trained blocks at a tenth of the learning rate, 8 epochs, weight averaging from epoch 5 with re-measured normalisation

implementation_brief:
Edit ONLY model/train.py. Leave model/model.py untouched, byte for byte.

1. Constants: add `JITTER_PX = 12  # max per-axis training-framing offset (half of dataset.STRIDE_PX = 24)` next to the other constants near CHUNK_SIZE. Import `_window_hits_holdout` from pipeline.dataset; it already exists there and list_crops uses it with signature (area, cx, cy, half_w). If importing a private name is awkward, import it anyway. It is read-only use of a frozen helper, and pipeline/ must NOT be edited.

2. In train_area(), right after `crop_xy = torch.tensor(...)` is built, precompute a per-position bool tensor `jit_ok` [N]. half_w = WINDOW_PX // 2 + 1 (= 92, the same as gpu_crops' hw). jit_ok[i] = True iff none of the four corner shifts (cx±JITTER_PX, cy±JITTER_PX) satisfies _window_hits_holdout(area, x, y, half_w). The holdout blocks are axis-aligned squares and the window is a square, so the four corners bound every shift inside the box. That is a one-time loop of ~72k×4 Python calls (seconds). Log the count: `[berlin] jitter ±12 px on N_ok/N positions (rest held at lattice: holdout buffer)`. Also store the raster bounds W = meta['width'], H = meta['height'].

3. chunk_views(meta, crop_xy, indices, rng, n_caps, jit_ok=None, jitter_px=0): if jitter_px > 0, draw dx, dy = rng.integers(-jitter_px, jitter_px + 1, size=len(indices)) (two independent draws, int64), zero them where jit_ok[indices] is False, then xy = xy + stack(dx, dy). Clamp xy[:,0] into [half_w, W - half_w] and xy[:,1] into [half_w, H - half_w], with half_w = WINDOW_PX // 2 + 1. gpu_crops indexes rows cy-hw .. cy+hw-1, so cy+hw <= H must hold. Check the inequality against gpu_crops and use the tighter bound if needed. Then proceed exactly as now: one offset per position, repeated across the n_caps captures via the existing rep(), the same as the shared heading. cells and pos are computed from the SHIFTED xy, which they already are if the shift is applied to xy before the existing lines. Keep the existing rng draw order for the heading (draw the angle first, then dx, dy), so the change is purely additive. With jitter_px=0 (the default), the behaviour must be byte-identical to today.

4. Pass jit_ok=jit_ok, jitter_px=JITTER_PX at both call sites: run_epoch (line ~406) and recalibrate_bn (line ~366). Thread jit_ok through their signatures, plus W and H if you do not read them from meta inside chunk_views; meta is already passed, so read meta['width'] and meta['height'] there. survey_diag must stay on the exact lattice. It does not call chunk_views today; confirm that and do not change it.

5. Logging: append `jitter=±{JITTER_PX}px` to the existing per-epoch line or the startup line, so the run log records it. Add a sentence to train.py's module docstring describing continuous-vantage jitter (capture-holdout era, experiment 22).

Unchanged and must stay so: model.py (architecture, MixStyle, cosine head, committee decode, loss_fn, export_onnx, estimate_position); AUG and augment_views; the paired-survey batching; EPOCHS, LR, TRUNK_LR_MULT, cosine schedule; WeightAverager (from epoch EPOCHS//2+1, every AVG_EVERY steps) and BN recalibration (BN_RECAL_BATCHES); make_soft_targets and residual_offset_target (they take pos, which is now the shifted centre, as intended).

Fixed contracts, restated: train.py keeps its CLI exactly. The harness calls it as it does today, and it reads ONLY buckets(meta, 'train'). Nothing under model/ may open the eval capture truedop_2024 in any form (that voids the experiment). It must export one ONNX per area at <out>/models/<area>.onnx, taking a 1x3x128x128 float32 input in [0,1] and returning [[u, v, conf]], with u, v normalised map coords and conf in [0,1], as documented in model/model.py's docstring. The export must pass pipeline/score.py's gates: fp32 ONNX ≤ 32 MiB (the current export is 31,693,415 bytes; this change adds no parameters) and a host latency proxy ≤ 250 ms (currently ~49 ms). Do not edit any /FROZEN file. Sanity check before finishing: run a short smoke test (e.g. the existing max_chunks timing path, or a tiny import-and-call of chunk_views) and confirm three things: shifted crops stay in bounds with no index error, pos equals the shifted centre, and jitter_px=0 reproduces the old xy.
